title: What does a 1:N model of a cargo UAV tell you about the 1:1 aircraft?
lede: research programme (proposal stage): per-quantity error budget for a Froude-scaled cargo aircraft model, with a stdlib scaling calculator; first-order result: at 1:10 the model needs 17 to 35% more power than Froude scaling predicts
summary: An open research programme on sub-scale flight testing of cargo and delivery aircraft. Dynamic (Froude) scaling keeps trim, mode frequencies and gust response, but Reynolds number falls as n<sup>1.5</sup>, so skin friction rises, and cell, motor and propeller performance do not scale with the airframe. The programme asks how large each error is for 1:2 to 1:20 models of an electric cargo aircraft, and whether a corrected model can recover it. Milestone 1 is a stdlib calculator (9 tests; exponent table dimensionally checked, ISA and Sutherland values checked) and a first-order flat-plate result for a 1,000 kg, aspect-ratio-10 airframe: at 1:10 the model needs 1.27× the Froude-scaled power (1.17 to 1.35 across form-factor, wetted-area and aspect-ratio sweeps) and L/D falls from 22.8 to 18.0. An untripped laminar-flow variant makes small models look better than full size, which is a modelling artefact and the reason the next milestones use XFOIL polars measured against UIUC data. The airframe constants are design choices, not a specific aircraft; the Froude exponents and the NASA TP-1435 and other citations are from memory and were not machine-checked (registries returned 403). Preliminary. Milestone 6a: on 134 measured cruise flights of a DJI Matrice 100 (Rodrigues et al. 2022 data, CC BY 4.0), electrical power scales with takeoff mass to the power 1.54 (95% bootstrap interval 1.41 to 1.67 over flights), consistent with the m<sup>1.5</sup> behind Froude power n<sup>3.5</sup>, within one airframe and a 13.6% mass range; electrical cruise power is 1.85× the ideal induced power at every payload, and falls 10% from 4 to 12 m/s. Payload is partly confounded with flight day (density not logged). Milestone 7a: at n = 0.2 the uncorrected model needs 1.157× the Froude power; a search of 178 section and boundary-layer cases (NACA 4-digit and low-Reynolds sections, CL within 6%, lift-curve slope within 5%) reaches at best 1.086, so no section restores it to within 5% (H5 refuted in this space; NeuralFoil polars, similarity kept).
